newsitem.title: JAPAN: Report says Japan, U.S., Germany plan forex action.
newsitem.headline: Report says Japan, U.S., Germany plan forex action.

text.p: Japan has made plans to take joint action with the United States and Germany to sell dollars for yen in the foreign exchange market to curb the rise in the U.S. currency, Kyodo news agency reported on Wednesday.

Quoting an international monetary source, Kyodo said Japanese authorities made preparations on Tuesday night for massive dollar-selling intervention with U.S. and German counterparts, but did not actually step in due to a U.S. request that the dollar's fluctuations be monitored further.
The Bank of Japan and Germany's Bundesbank both declined to comment on the Kyodo report.
"We do not comment on rumours," a Bundesbank spokeswoman said. "The Bundesbank stands by the statement made at the G7."

The Group of Seven (G7) nations said in Washington last week that exchange rates should reflect economic fundamentals and that excessive fluctuations were undesirable. They agreed to monitor exchange rates and cooperate as appropriate in the currency markets.
The source told Kyodo that Japanese authorities were still hoping for concerted intervention and adding that Tokyo would continue to try to "act at the best time".
The dollar briefly dipped to below 125 yen in early European trading after the report, traders said.
